PLAINTIFF’S PROTECTIVE OPPOSITION TO
DEFENDANT KATIE HALL’S MOTION TO DISMISS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine files this opposition protectively: it demonstrates that the
First Amended Complaint (“FAC”) states its claims on the facts already pleaded, without awaiting,
and without prejudice to, Plaintiff’s pending motion for leave to file a supplemental pleading under
Rule 15(d). ECF No. 26.

I. HALL’S MOTION PRESENTS THE SAME GROUNDS ALREADY

BRIEFED

Hall’s motion adopts ECF Nos. 10 and 11 and seeks dismissal on the same grounds asserted

by NCMEC: litigation privilege, federal statutory immunity, truth and falsity, defamation by

implication, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and conspiracy.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document51_ Filed 09/03/26 Page 2 of 5 PagelD# 447

ECF No. 30 responds to the corresponding arguments contained in ECF No. 11. Hall’s
adoption therefore places before the Court the same Rule 12 issues Plaintiff has already
substantively answered.

II. PLAINTIFF RELIES UPON HIS EXISTING RESPONSES TO THE

ARGUMENTS HALL HAS ADOPTED

Plaintiff relies upon the arguments set forth in ECF No. 30, to the extent applicable to Hall,
as his opposition to the corresponding arguments Hall has adopted from ECF No. 11.

Plaintiff maintains against Hall each response made in ECF No. 30 concerning litigation
privilege, statutory immunity, truth and falsity, defamation by implication, intentional infliction of
emotional distress, and conspiracy.

Plaintiff opposes ECF No. 45 in its entirety. Each argument asserted in ECF No. 30 against
a corresponding ground in ECF No. 11 is asserted here against Hall’s adoption of that ground. The
abbreviated form of this filing reflects that those substantive issues have already been briefed.

I. HALL’S ADOPTION DOES NOT ALTER THE ISSUES ALREADY

PRESENTED

Hall’s adoption changes the movant asserting the arguments; it does not change the
arguments themselves. By adopting ECF No. 11, Hall invokes the same contentions concerning
litigation privilege, statutory immunity, truth, defamation by implication, intentional infliction of
emotional distress, and conspiracy that Plaintiff has already answered.

Plaintiff’s existing responses therefore apply to Hall’s motion with equal force. ECF No.
45 supplies no separate substantive ground for dismissal beyond those already addressed in ECF

No. 30.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document51_ Filed 09/03/26 Page 3 of 5 PagelD# 448

This opposition is directed to ECF No. 45 as presently framed against the First Amended
Complaint. Plaintiff separately seeks leave to File Supplemental Complaint pursuant to Federal
Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d). Plaintiff preserves his Rule 15 motion and the supplemental
pleading.

Iv. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons and for the reasons stated in Plaintiff’s existing opposition to the
arguments Hall has adopted, ECF No. 30, Defendant Katie Hall’s Motion to Dismiss should be
denied. Plaintiff’s request is made protectively and without prejudice to his pending Motion for

Leave under Rule 15(d) and the resulting pleading posture if that motion is granted.
